filesToTouch.what: Add pure UTC day primitives beside `isRealDate`, all set-agnostic and free of any live-animals knowledge: `startOfUtcDay(date)` (midnight UTC), `addUtcDays(date, days)`, `addUtcMonths(date, months)` clamped to the last day of the target month (31/8 + 6 months is 28/2 or 29/2, never 3/3), `parseDateText(raw)` returning a UTC Date or null for a d/m/yyyy or dd/mm/yyyy string that is a real calendar date, and `formatDateText(date)` returning `d/m/yyyy` with no leading zeros — the format the MoJ picker itself emits via `formattedDateFromDate` when `leadingZeros` is unset. Reuse `parseDateText` inside the existing `dateText` path rather than leaving the regex duplicated.

Add `dateTextInRange(name, { min, max, invalidMessage, rangeMessage })` modelled on the existing `integerInRange` idiom: blank passes (the range rule must not turn an optional field into a required one), a value that is not a real d/m/yyyy calendar date fails with `invalidMessage`, and a real date outside the inclusive `[min, max]` Date bounds fails with `rangeMessage`. `min`/`max` are `Date` objects supplied by the caller — no clock read and no date policy inside L2. Leave `dateText` behaviour untouched; exit-date and documents keep using it.
Export `dateTextInRange` alongside `dateText` and `dateParts`.

Add a `#dateTextInRange` describe beside the existing `#dateText` one, following its style: blank accepted; the exact min and max boundary dates accepted (inclusive); one day below min and one day above max rejected with `rangeMessage`; a calendar-impossible value such as `31/2/2026` rejected with `invalidMessage` rather than the range message; bounds passed as fixed `Date` literals so the test never reads the clock.

Extend `dateField(name, { label, hint, value, error, minDate, maxDate })` to carry `minDate` and `maxDate` straight into the returned view model so `mojDatePicker` emits `data-min-date`/`data-max-date` on the wrapper div. Stay a pure view-model builder: no clock read, no date arithmetic, no live-animals policy. When the bounds are absent the returned object must be unchanged from today so the exit-date and documents pickers stay unrestricted per the ruling.

New L2 unit spec for `dateField`: given `minDate`/`maxDate` the view model carries them verbatim; given neither, both keys are absent (or undefined) so the macro emits no restriction attributes. This is the file that pins the ruling's 'exit date and date of issue get NO restriction' half.

ruling: RULED 2026-08-10 (Sam) — CORRECTED, supersedes the earlier reading of this gate. APPLY the arrival-date restriction: the field that HAS a ticket specifying it is precisely the one to restrict. Per EUDPA-309, arrivalDateAtPort accepts earliest 1 week before today and latest 6 months after today; an out-of-range value typed manually must be REJECTED server-side with an error summary and an inline message, not merely greyed out in the calendar; the control degrades to a usable text input with JavaScript off; the stored date shape is unchanged. exitDate and accompanyingDocumentDateOfIssue get NO restriction for now — both accept any valid date, and no validation is to be added for them. This increment is therefore real work, not a no-op. COORDINATION RISK the re-specifier must resolve before specifying: EUDPA-309 is Ready for Dev and assigned to Hamid Jemei, and covers replacing the arrival date input with the MOJ picker. This snag says the MOJ picker is already in use but unrestricted. Establish from the code which is true today, and scope this increment to the restriction ONLY — do not re-do the control swap if it has already landed, and do not duplicate work sitting in someone else's ticket.
